title: The Firmament
text: WHEN I survey the bright Celestial sphere: So rich with jewels hung, that night Doth like an Ethiop bride appear. My soul her wings doth spread, And Heaven-ward flies, The Almighty's mysteries to read In the large volumes of the skies. For the bright firmament Shoots forth no flame So silent, but is eloquent In speaking the Creator's name. No unregarded star Contracts its light Into so small a character Remov'd far from our humane sight: But if we steadfast look, We shall discern In it, as in some holy book, How man may heavenly knowledge learn. Thus those celestial fires, Though seeming mute, The fallacy of our desires And all the pride of life confute. For they have watched since first The world had birth; And found sin in itself accurst, And nothing permanent on earth.
